correctness.rationale: A unit-modulus 3-by-3 determinant vanishes iff two rows or columns are proportional, proved by normalizing and comparing conjugated products. For \(F_p^2\), this means row or column difference annihilates the three-point other support direction. Triangular rows have three distinct annihilating directions with exactly p binom(p,3) column triples each, all rank two. Linear rows are separated by one linear functional; its one/two/three-valued fibers yield ranks one/two/three, with exact counts. Summing produces R_1,R_2,R_3 for every prime p>=3. Separately executed exact cyclotomic determinant and 2x2 minor checker enumerates every pair at p=3,5 and passes. Computation alone does not establish all-prime quantification.

value.rationale: The smallest nonlinear square Fourier minors relevant to restricted interpolation and exponential bases are 3x3. The complete incidence pattern of the noncyclic prime-plane character table gives a natural full rank distribution for every prime, with a structural orthogonal-direction explanation and distinct fixed-support behavior for collinear versus triangular row sets. The answer is not determined by existing uncertainty support-cardinality bounds or by the cyclic prime-square table. A stand-alone classification of this natural invariant is valuable without a downstream theorem. The exact (p+1)-fold scaling of rank deficiencies relative to the nonisomorphic cyclic prime-square character table is an additional structural comparison.
